newsitem.title: THAILAND: IFCT sees Thai economic growth at 6.4 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: IFCT sees Thai economic growth at 6.4 pct in 1996.

text.p: Thailand is set to post its lowest economic growth for a decade this year at 6.4 percent, the Industrial Finance Corp of Thailand Plc said on Thursday.

Economic growth as measured by the gross domestic product (GDP) in 1995 was 8.6 percent. The state-backed bank also said the current account deficit for 1996 was set to rise to 8.6 percent of GDP versus 8.1 percent in 1995.
However, the IFCT saw an improvement in the indicators next year with economic growth estimated at 7.2 percent and the current account deficit falling as a percentage of GDP to 8.2 percent in 1997.

The projections were released at an IFCT forum on the outlook for the Thai economy. Confidence in the economy has been hit by a growing current account deficit problem. The IFCT said export growth, which has faltered this year, will decline to 1.4 percent growth in 1996 from 24 percent in 1995.

Import growth is set to rise by 8.5 percent in 1997 from 5.6 percent this year, though the trade deficit as a percentage of GDP will decline to 9.2 percent in 1997 from 9.8 percent this year, the bank said.
